h1: Retatrutide vs tirzepatide: no trial has compared them in people, and what that means for every number you have seen
dek: One is an approved medicine with a 2,539-person phase 3 trial behind it; the other is investigational, with one phase 2 trial in 338 people. The figures that circulate come from putting those two trials side by side, which is not a comparison. This page tables what each trial did, quotes the only indirect estimates that exist, and says what follows.

queries.heading: Does retatrutide cost more muscle than tirzepatide?
queries.answer: Neither trial reported body composition in its main results, and no study has compared the two on lean mass. What is known is that large, fast weight loss of any cause takes lean tissue with fat, and that this is measured in some trials of these drugs and not in others. Anyone quoting a lean-mass difference between retatrutide and tirzepatide is comparing studies that did not measure the same thing.

queries.heading: How long do they last in the body?
queries.answer: Both are once-weekly injections. Retatrutide's half-life was about six days in its early trials, which is what supports weekly dosing. Tirzepatide's is around five days, with the same consequence. In practice the difference matters less than the escalation schedule, which is many weeks long for both.

queries.heading: Does retatrutide cause hair loss?
queries.answer: Hair shedding is reported after rapid weight loss of any cause, including after bariatric surgery, and it is described in trials of several of these drugs. No trial has compared retatrutide and tirzepatide on it, and no abstract in this ledger reports a rate for either.

queries.heading: What about heart rate?
queries.answer: Small increases in heart rate are a known class effect of incretin drugs, and the glucagon receptor activity that makes retatrutide a triple agonist is the part with the least long-term human data. The phase 2 trial reported dose-dependent increases in heart rate that were largest in the first half of the trial. Longer-term cardiovascular outcomes are what phase 3 is for, and they are not yet published.

queries.heading: How quickly does retatrutide work?
queries.answer: In the phase 2 trial the weight curve was still falling at the end. Average loss at 24 weeks was 17.5% on the highest dose and 24.2% at 48 weeks, so half the effect came in the second half of the trial. Both drugs also start with a long escalation, so the first weeks are about tolerating the dose rather than reaching it.

information_gain: The only page on this query that states the central fact, that no trial has ever given both drugs to the same people, and then shows why the circulating comparison fails: the retatrutide figure comes from a 48-week phase 2 trial in 338 adults and the tirzepatide figure from a 72-week phase 3 trial in 2,539 adults, a difference of 24 weeks on a weight curve that was still falling. The only page to quote the indirect estimates that do exist, from a 2026 network meta-analysis of 58 trials, with their confidence intervals and its own warning about overlapping intervals and limited head-to-head evidence. The only page to show what the eight studies in its own ledger that name both drugs actually are, including that the single study to give both to the same subjects was in mice at 10 nmol/kg. And the only page to note that a 2023 commentary in the investigational-drugs literature named the missing tirzepatide comparison as the thing retatrutide needed, three years ago.
serp_format_rewarded: A cited comparison with tables. The top ten is telehealth marketing with two to four citations each; the one page with real references ranks eleventh, and a conference abstract ranks fourth, so the query tolerates primary literature. A trial table and an explicit statement of what is not known is the gap.
open_actions: Add the phase 3 TRIUMPH programme registrations to the ledger when results publish; the page states that they are ongoing from the trial registry, editorially.
